build_inputs.angles:
1. Lead on this: the engine revs to 7,800 rpm and this is the last base 911
that does it without turbochargers. 3.4 litres, 350 horsepower at 7,400 rpm,
naturally aspirated. In 2017 the base car moved to a turbocharged 3.0 and the
redline came down to 7,500. Every base 911 built since has had turbos, so 2015
is the end of that line and Porsche has not gone back.

2. Cover the reversal, because it is the most interesting thing about this car.
When it launched the reviews complained: Porsche had thrown out hydraulic
steering for an electromechanical rack, and evo said the new steering was like
listening to an MP3 of the 997's. Purists said the feel was gone. Ten years on
nobody makes that complaint, because the car that replaced this one has turbos,
and the steering argument looks small beside the engine argument. The 911 they
moaned about is now the one they are hunting for.

3. Cover the catch, and be straight that it is the good kind. This is the 9A1
engine - no IMS bearing, which is the thing that scares people off a 996 or an
early 997, and bore scoring is rare on the 3.4 rather than an expected risk.
What does break is duller and cheaper: the cooling-system valves and sensors
fail often enough that specialists expect them - no heat, the sports exhaust
refuses to switch, a cooling-system fault on the dash - and the camshaft-driven
high-pressure fuel pump can go. So the famous 911 engine fear does not apply to
this one, and what you budget for instead is plumbing.

4. Mention the gearbox. Seven-speed manual, which Porsche claimed as a first
for a production car (verify independently). The PDK is the quicker one - 4.4
seconds to sixty against 4.6 for the manual - and the manual is the one that
holds its money, because a naturally aspirated 911 with three pedals is the
whole reason to want this generation now.

5. Close by putting it against a new base 911. Do not give the price of this car
yourself - use the verified comparable sales. The point is what the money buys:
a new base 911 is a turbocharged 3.0, and the thing it cannot sell you at any
price is this engine.

script: This was the last naturally aspirated version before the base car went turbocharged. It's the 2015 Porsche 911 Carrera Coupe; US cars stayed naturally aspirated through 2016 before twin turbos arrived for 2017. Its direct-injected 3.4-liter flat-six uses integrated dry-sump lubrication and makes 350 horsepower at 7,400 rpm and 287 pound-feet of torque. But when this generation arrived, reviewers complained that electric steering filtered out feedback they'd loved in the hydraulic 997. That was the original controversy. Then Porsche downsized the base engine to a turbocharged 3.0, which makes this earlier car's lack of boost the draw. Porsche changed the argument. This one's seven-speed PDK dual-clutch gearbox sends power to the rear wheels and reaches sixty in 4.4 seconds. They're going for about $67,000 on the market today. Would you take this naturally aspirated engine over the turbocharged engine Porsche put in the base car that followed?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2015 Porsche 911 Carrera Coupe, finished in black with a black interior. The odometer on this 911 currently displays approximately 35,800 miles. This Porsche has reportedly been registered in Florida and California since 2018. According to the build sheet provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes the Bose Audio Package, 20-inch Carrera S wheels, SportDesign side mirrors, and instrument dials and seat belts in Guards Red. Notable modifications reported by the seller include a SOUL Performance muffler, Öhlins Road & Track DFV coilovers, an aftermarket front lip, an aftermarket steering wheel, and Apple CarPlay compatibility. Porsche introduced the 991-generation 911 for the 2012 model year. It arrived as an evolution of its predecessor, the 997, and it received more powerful engines across the board and a more luxurious interior. It was longer, lower, and wider — and it relied extensively on aluminum to avoid putting on weight. Power comes from a 3.4-liter flat-6, rated at 350 horsepower and 287 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission.
